description: Use one canned base, one jarred flavour driver, and one green vegetable to build an easy pantry pasta dinner with the 1-1-1 method.
h1: The 1-1-1 Pantry Pasta Method: Build Dinner From a Tin, a Jar, and a Green
intro: A weeknight pasta can start with three small decisions: one canned base, one jarred flavour driver, and one green vegetable. The 1-1-1 method gives those ingredients a clear job, then lets you choose a pasta shape and finish that suit what is already around.
The result is a dinner route rather than a rigid recipe. Use it when you have a tin of beans, tuna, or tomatoes; a jar that can bring punch; and a green that needs a place on the plate.

sections.heading: The 1-1-1 setup
paragraphs: Choose one ingredient from each column.

rows: Cannellini beans, chickpeas, lentils, tuna, tomatoes
Pesto, olive tapenade, roasted peppers, sun-dried tomatoes, capers
Spinach, kale, broccoli, peas, green beans, rocket

paragraphs_after: Add pasta, olive oil, garlic or onion if you have it, and a final element such as lemon, cheese, breadcrumbs, or herbs.

sections.heading: Match the pasta to the route
paragraphs: The shape can help the ingredients feel like one dinner instead of a bowl of separate add-ons.

rows: Torn greens and a spoonful of pesto
Chilli flakes and a sharp cheese

paragraphs_after: Use whatever pasta you have. The table is a nudge for texture, not a rulebook.

sections.heading: 1. White beans + pesto + spinach
paragraphs: Warm garlic in olive oil, add drained white beans, then loosen pesto with a little pasta water. Fold in spinach at the end and toss with shells or short tubes. Lemon keeps the finish lively.

sections.heading: 2. Tuna + roasted peppers + green beans
paragraphs: Slice roasted peppers and warm them with garlic and olive oil. Add tuna in generous flakes, then toss through spaghetti with blanched green beans. A handful of breadcrumbs gives the plate a welcome crunch.

sections.heading: 3. Chickpeas + sun-dried tomatoes + kale
paragraphs: Chop sun-dried tomatoes finely so they season the oil. Add chickpeas, a splash of pasta water, and ribbons of kale. Orecchiette catches the small pieces beautifully. Finish with cheese or a squeeze of lemon.

sections.heading: 4. Tomatoes + capers + peas
paragraphs: Simmer canned tomatoes briefly with capers, then add peas while the sauce bubbles. Toss with rigatoni and finish with herbs if you have them. This route leans bright, briny, and saucy.

sections.heading: A five-step cooking sequence
paragraphs: Taste as you go. Jarred ingredients bring different levels of salt, oil, and acidity, so the last adjustment belongs at the table.
steps: Put the pasta water on first.
Start the flavour driver in olive oil: chop, blend, or warm it as needed.
Add the canned base and enough pasta water to make a light sauce.
Add the green at the moment it needs: earlier for broccoli or beans, later for spinach, rocket, or herbs.
Toss everything with the pasta and choose one finishing element for contrast in texture or brightness.

sections.heading: When the cupboard looks mismatched
paragraphs: A useful order of operations keeps dinner moving:
That is enough structure for a real dinner, even when the ingredient list looks a little random at first glance.
list: Start with the tin that needs a job.
Pick the jarred ingredient that can season it.
Choose the green that works with the cooking time you have.
Let pasta shape and finishing ingredients solve the rest.

sections.heading: Make the method yours
paragraphs: The 1-1-1 method is built for small variations. Swap the green, change the jar, or use a different pasta shape next time. Keeping a few flexible ingredients visible makes these dinner routes easier to spot.
Open your kitchen, choose one ingredient for each part of the 1-1-1 method, and make tonight's pasta route your own.
